questions.q: According to the capstone requirements, what must AIClient's error handling do?
options: Retry every single error type exactly the same way
Ignore all errors silently
Use custom exceptions and a retry loop that only retries transient failures
Never raise any exceptions at all
questions.explain: Requirement 2 calls for resilient error handling: custom exceptions plus a retry loop that distinguishes transient failures from ones that will never succeed.

questions.q: Which capstone requirement does Lesson 20 (testing) map to?
options: A tested retry path — at least one mocked test proving a 429 followed by success recovers
Clean class design in __init__
Reading rate-limit headers
Correct request/response handling
questions.explain: Requirement 4 explicitly requires a mocked test proving the retry logic actually works, which is what Lesson 20 taught.

questions.q: According to this lesson, are streaming and tool calling required for the capstone to count as done?
options: Yes, both are strict requirements
No — they're strong additions / stretch goals, not strict requirements
Only tool calling is required, not streaming
Neither topic is relevant to this capstone at all
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly separates the five required items from streaming and tool calling, which are called out as strong additions rather than requirements.

questions.q: What does requirement 5, 'clean class design,' actually require, per Lesson 17?
options: Every method must be a static method
No comments anywhere in the code
Shared config set up once in __init__, with one method per real action
The class must have exactly one method
questions.explain: Lesson 17's design principle — shared setup in __init__, thin focused methods — is what requirement 5 is asking the capstone to demonstrate.

questions.q: Per this lesson, what does a finished capstone look like to another developer?
options: They must read the entire source file to understand how to use it
It only works if they already took this exact course
They can use AIClient just from its method names and docstrings, without reading the source first
It requires a live API key to even read the code
questions.explain: The lesson's definition of 'done' includes being usable by another developer through clear method names and docstrings alone.
